zh: 固定一个窗口，其中的 0 不用处理；每个正数要么花 1 次操作 2 直接清零，要么花 a[i] 次操作 1。显然应该把操作 2 用在窗口里最大的若干个数上。
窗口向左扩展时，“去掉最大的 Y 个之后剩余正数之和”只增不减，所以对每个右端点，合法左端点构成一段后缀，可以用双指针。窗口内的正数用两个有序多重集合维护：top 存最大的至多 Y 个，rest 存其余并记录其和 restSum。
右端加入正数时先放进 top，超过 Y 个就把 top 中最小的移到 rest（restSum 加上它）；当 restSum>X 时移出左端元素：若它在 rest 中直接删并减 restSum，否则从 top 删，并把 rest 中最大的补回 top；每个右端点用窗口长度更新答案；restSum 用 64 位整数。
en: Fix a window: its zeros need nothing, and each positive number either costs one operation 2 or a[i] operations 1. Clearly operation 2 should go to the largest numbers in the window.

When the window extends to the left, the sum of the positives left after removing the largest Y only grows, so for each right end the valid left ends form a suffix and two pointers work. Keep the window's positives in two ordered multisets: top holds the largest at most Y values, rest holds the others with their sum restSum.

When the right end adds a positive value, insert it into top; if top has more than Y values, move its smallest into rest (adding it to restSum); while restSum > X remove the left element: if it is in rest, delete it and subtract it from restSum, otherwise delete it from top and move the largest value of rest back to top; update the answer with the window length for every right end; keep restSum in 64-bit integers.

explanationEn:
## Problem

Operation 1 decreases one element by 1, at most X times; operation 2 sets one element directly to 0, at most Y times. Find the longest contiguous subarray that can become all zeros.

## Approach

Fix a window. Its zeros need no work; every positive number costs either one operation 2 or a[i] operations 1. The best choice is to spend the Y operations 2 on the largest positive numbers in the window, and the sum of the remaining positives must not exceed X.

When the window extends to the left, "the sum after removing the largest Y" never decreases, so for each right end the valid left ends form a suffix and two pointers can be used. Maintain the positive numbers in the window with two ordered multisets: top holds the largest at most Y values, rest holds the others and records their sum restSum. When the right end adds an element, put it in top first; if top exceeds Y elements, move the smallest of top into rest. When the left end removes an element, delete it directly if it is in rest; otherwise delete it from top and move the largest of rest back into top. While restSum > X, move the left end to the right.

## Correctness

Exchange argument: if a smaller positive number uses operation 2 while a larger one does not, swapping how the two are handled keeps the number of operations 2 the same and does not increase the number of operations 1, so an optimal plan always gives operation 2 to the largest Y values. The two sets always satisfy that every element of top is at least every element of rest and |top| = min(Y, number of positives), so restSum is exactly the minimum cost. Monotonicity ensures the two pointers miss no solution.

## Complexity

O(n log n). restSum can reach the order of 10^14, so use 64-bit integers.

## Independent verification

The oracle sorts every window and directly computes "the sum after removing the largest Y" (O(n^2 log n)), without two pointers or sets. Even smaller data is additionally checked with a step-by-step state search over operations (array, X used, Y used), validating the model "operation 2 goes to the largest values" itself. All inputs with length 1..4, elements 0..3, X in 0..3 and Y in 0..2 are enumerated and each is run through the actual reference program. The wrong solutions cover giving operation 2 to the earliest elements, treating operation 1 as a single clear, ignoring operation 1, and 32-bit accumulation.
